text: Chris Nwabueze Ngige (born 8 August 1952) is a Nigerian politician and medical doctor who served as Minister of Labour and Employment under President Muhammadu Buhari from 2015 to 2023. He was elected Senator for Anambra Central Constituency in April 2011. Ngige was governor of Anambra State from May 2003 to March 2006 under the People's Democratic Party (PDP). A medical doctor by profession, he graduated from the University of Nigeria-Nsukka in 1979 and served in the civil service, including at the National Assembly and state house clinics, retiring in 1998 as deputy director in the Federal Ministry of Health. He joined the PDP in 1999, serving as Assistant National Secretary and Zonal Secretary in the South East region. His 2003 gubernatorial election was controversial, and after an unsuccessful attempt on 10 July 2003 to have him removed via a fabricated resignation letter accepted by the state assembly, he broke ranks with his political godfather, Chris Uba, brother of Andy Uba. In August 2006, an Election Tribunal led by Justice Nabaruma nullified Ngige's 2003 victory, and the Nigerian Federal Court of Appeal confirmed the annulment on 15 March 2006, awarding the win to Peter Obi of the All Progressives Grand Alliance (APGA). Ngige accepted the judgment in good faith and called on the people of Anambra to support Obi. Following Obi's impeachment, which was later overturned, Ngige attempted to run for governor in April 2007 but was disqualified by the Independent National Electoral Commission, despite a Federal High Court voiding the disqualification; Obi ultimately served out his term. Ngige faced criticism for appearing naked at the Okija voodoo shrine during his gubernatorial campaign. On 6 February 2010, he contested again for governor, facing 25 candidates including Andy Uba, Charles Soludo, Nicholas Ukachukwu, Mrs. Uche Ekwunife, Ralph Nwosu, and incumbent Peter Obi, who won the election. In April 2011, Ngige ran for senator on the Action Congress of Nigeria (ACN) platform, winning with 69,765 votes to Professor Dora Akunyili's 69,292 after voting issues in some areas led to a re-vote on 25 April. His senatorial tenure ended when he lost the 2015 election to Hon. Mrs Uche Ekwunife, who was sworn in as senator for Anambra Central in the 8th National Assembly. On 11 November 2015, Ngige was appointed Minister of Labour and Employment by President Muhammadu Buhari. In 2019, he was nominated by President Buhari for screening by the National Assembly and was sworn in on 21 August 2019 as Minister of Labour and Employment. On 19 April 2022, Ngige declared interest in running for President of Nigeria under the All Progressive Congress (APC) banner, describing himself as "jack of all trade and masters of all". His 2003 gubernatorial election was annulled in March 2006 by the Court of Appeal, which declared Peter Obi the rightful winner, and a 2012 profile noted the annulment was based on "electoral malpractice". On 12 December 2025, Ngige was arraigned before the Federal Capital Territory High Court in Gwarinpa, Abuja, on an eight-count charge filed by the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC). The charges relate to his tenure as supervising minister of the Nigeria Social Insurance Trust Fund (NSITF) between September 2015 and May 2023, alleging he conferred unfair advantages on companies linked to his associates through contract awards under Sections 19 and 17(a) of the Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Act, 2000. Ngige is also accused of corruptly accepting monetary gifts totaling ₦119.78 million from contractors, allegedly funneled through the "Dr Chris Nwabueze Ngige Campaign Organisation" and the "Senator (Dr) Chris Ngige Scholarship Scheme". Ngige pleaded not guilty to all charges.
